checked_sources.evidence: Opened IAU page; lines 48-61 establish bounded sky regions and that constellation stars are not necessarily physically connected; line 148 identifies Lepus/Lep.

Opened ESA IC 418 page; lines 9-13 support the Lepus direction, ~2,000 light-years, planetary-nebula stage, red-giant mass loss, ~0.2-light-year diameter and UV fluorescence; line 16 says Hubble texture origin remains uncertain.

articles.notes: The self-check accurately distinguishes distance from nebular diameter and explains UV-driven fluorescence.

checked_sources.evidence: Opened IAU page; lines 48-61 define the bounded region / nonphysical star-pattern distinction; line 168 identifies Puppis/Pup.

Opened NASA M46 page; lines 295-317 identify M46/NGC 2437 as an open cluster in Puppis at 5,400 light-years and NGC 2438 as a foreground nebula 2,400 light-years closer; lines 319-321 describe the dying Sun-like star, nebula and white dwarf.

articles.notes: The self-check correctly treats projected proximity as insufficient evidence of physical membership.

checked_sources.evidence: Opened IAU page; lines 48-61 support the bounded-area concept and distinction from a physical cluster; line 161 identifies Pavo/Pav.

Opened ESA/Hubble NGC 6752 image page; lines 0-4 support use of white dwarfs to measure cluster age and discovery of background galaxy Bedin 1 as faint stars; lines 23-27 explicitly associate NGC 6752 with Pavo.

articles.notes: The self-check correctly keeps Bedin 1 separate from the globular cluster and explains the white-dwarf age study.

checked_sources.evidence: Opened IAU page; lines 48-61 define the 88 bounded regions and nonphysical pattern distinction; line 122 identifies Chamaeleon/Cha.

Opened NASA IC 2631 release; lines 250-253 support the IC 2631 protostar and Chamaeleon association, collapse/accretion heating before fusion, and infrared visibility because dust obscures visible light.

articles.notes: The self-check accurately explains pre-fusion heat and why infrared observations are useful.
